title: The Kingdom Beyond the Mist
content:
The mist had covered the northern valley for more than a century.

According to the oldest chronicles, it had appeared on the morning King Aldren was murdered. By sunset, the entire valley had vanished beneath an impenetrable veil of silver fog, and every attempt to cross it had ended in failure.

Some explorers had returned days later without remembering where they had been.

Others had never returned at all.

The people of the surrounding kingdoms eventually stopped searching for answers.

But on the morning of her twenty-fifth birthday, Princess Elara received a letter bearing the royal seal of a kingdom that officially no longer existed.

She broke the wax carefully.

Inside, there was only one sentence.

When the moon rises tonight, you will cross the mist.

Elara read it twice.

Then she walked directly to the royal library.

Her older brother, Adrian, was already there.

— You received one too, didn't you? — she asked.

He looked up.

— How did you know?

She placed the letter on the table.

His expression changed.

— So it has begun.

— What has begun?

Adrian closed the ancient book he had been reading.

— The return.

Elara stared at him.

— You know what this means?

— I know what the chronicles say.

— Then tell me.

He hesitated.

— Beyond the mist, there will be a kingdom.

— A dead kingdom.

— Not dead.

He looked toward the library window.

— Waiting.

That evening, Elara stood at the edge of the valley.

The mist stretched before her like a vast, shifting wall. No wind disturbed it. No sound came from beyond it.

Her brother approached carrying a lantern.

— You will not go alone.

— Father will never allow you to come.

— Father doesn't know.

Elara smiled.

— That's probably why you're my favorite brother.

— I'm your only brother.

— That makes the competition easier.

Adrian laughed.

Then his expression became serious.

— Once we enter, we won't know what we'll find.

— We'll find the truth.

— Perhaps.

He handed her the lantern.

— Keep this lit.

— Why?

— The old stories say the mist will imitate the voices of people we trust.

Elara frowned.

— And what will happen if we listen?

Adrian looked into the fog.

— We will follow the voice.

— And then?

— We will disappear.

Elara tightened her grip on the lantern.

— Then we won't listen.

They stepped forward.

The mist swallowed them.

For several minutes, they walked in complete silence.

The world beyond the fog seemed distorted. Trees appeared where there had been none, and distant lights flickered between the branches.

Then Elara heard her father's voice.

— Elara.

She stopped.

Adrian grabbed her arm.

— Don't turn around.

The voice came again.

— Elara, come back.

She closed her eyes.

— That's not him.

— I know.

The voice changed.

This time, it sounded like her mother.

— My child, you will be safe if you return.

Elara's heart tightened.

Her mother had died when she was ten.

— Keep walking — Adrian whispered.

They continued.

Soon, the fog began to thin.

A magnificent city emerged before them.

Its towers were made of pale stone. Silver banners hung from enormous bridges. Strange blue lights floated above the streets.

But there were no people.

Elara stared.

— This place can't be real.

— It is.

They entered the city.

The streets were immaculate, as though they had been abandoned only minutes earlier.

Then they reached a vast palace.

Its doors opened by themselves.

Inside, a woman was waiting.

She wore a crown of black crystal.

— Welcome, Princess Elara.

Adrian stepped forward.

— Who are you?

The woman smiled.

— Queen Seraphine.

Elara looked around.

— This is the lost kingdom.

— It was.

— What happened here?

Seraphine turned toward the throne.

— Your ancestor betrayed us.

Elara felt a chill.

— King Aldren?

— He feared what we had become.

— What did you become?

The queen's expression darkened.

— Powerful.

She raised her hand.

The walls changed.

Images appeared across the stone: armies, enchanted forests, enormous creatures flying above cities, and sorcerers commanding storms.

— Your ancestor wanted our magic.

— And he destroyed the kingdom?

— He sealed it.

Elara stared at the images.

— Why bring me here?

Seraphine approached her.

— Because the seal will break tonight.

Adrian stepped forward.

— What will happen?

The queen looked at him.

— The kingdom will return.

A distant bell rang.

Once.

Twice.

Three times.

The palace trembled.

— And what will happen to our kingdom? — Elara asked.

Seraphine smiled.

— It will become part of ours.

Elara's expression hardened.

— You expect me to allow that?

— You will not have a choice.

The queen raised her hand.

Darkness spread across the floor.

Adrian drew his sword.

— Run!

They fled through the palace corridors.

Behind them, the sound of stone cracking echoed through the building.

— Where will we go? — Adrian shouted.

— I don't know!

— That's reassuring!

They reached a balcony overlooking the city.

The mist was disappearing.

Beyond it, Elara could see the distant lights of her own kingdom.

Then she noticed something beneath the balcony.

A colossal stone gate stood at the center of the city.

Symbols were glowing across its surface.

— That's the source.

Adrian looked at her.

— The source of what?

— The seal.

She pointed toward the gate.

— If we destroy it, the kingdom won't return.

Adrian stared at the enormous structure.

— How will we reach it?

Elara looked toward the palace.

— We will jump.

— That's your plan?

— Do you have a better one?

He looked down.

— No.

— Then follow me.

They climbed onto the balcony railing.

— Elara!

She jumped.

For one terrifying moment, there was nothing beneath her.

Then a powerful gust of wind lifted her.

She landed safely on a lower bridge.

Adrian followed.

Together, they ran toward the gate.

Seraphine appeared behind them.

— You will regret this!

Elara turned.

— Perhaps.

She reached the gate.

The symbols were burning now.

She placed both hands against the stone.

The ancient language suddenly became understandable.

A single sentence appeared.

The blood of the king will decide the fate of the kingdom.

Elara understood.

The seal had been created through her ancestor's blood.

And it could only be broken—or renewed—by his descendant.

Seraphine approached slowly.

— You will open the gate.

— No.

— You will.

Elara looked at Adrian.

Then she understood what the queen had not.

The gate did not require her blood.

It required a choice.

She pressed her hand against the final symbol.

— I will choose to seal it again.

The entire city shook.

Light erupted from the gate.

Seraphine screamed as the palace began collapsing into mist.

— You cannot erase us!

Elara shouted back:

— I won't erase you.

She looked at the ancient city.

— I will give you another chance.

The light intensified.

The kingdom disappeared.

The mist returned.

Then everything became silent.

At sunrise, Elara and Adrian emerged from the valley.

The mist had vanished completely.

Behind them stood only an empty valley covered in silver grass.

Their father and the royal guards were waiting.

— Where have you been? — the king demanded.

Elara looked toward the mountains.

— Finding the truth.

Adrian smiled.

— And saving everyone from it.

The king frowned.

— What does that mean?

Elara looked at the horizon.

— It means the past will no longer control us.

She knew the kingdom beyond the mist had not truly disappeared.

One day, the seal would weaken again.

One day, someone would return.

And when that day came, Elara would be ready.

She would study the ancient language.

She would learn the magic her ancestors had feared.

She would search for the people who had been trapped beyond the mist for generations.

And if they returned peacefully, she would welcome them.

If they returned as enemies, she would defend her kingdom.

But for now, she would let the valley sleep.

The future would come soon enough.

And when it did, she would decide what kind of queen she would become.
